questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Georgia about 69,700 square kilometres; Estonia about 45,335 square kilometres; Taiwan about 36,197 square kilometres; North Macedonia about 25,713 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Georgia?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Georgia on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Georgia article.

questions.proof: It is situated on the coast of the Black Sea and borders Russia to the north, Turkey and Armenia to the south, and Azerbaijan to the southeast.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Georgia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Georgia article.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Georgia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Georgia is the Georgian lari.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Tbilisi?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Georgia is Tbilisi.
